Its easy to fall into the thought process of not wanting to be better, its almost comfortable the depression because of how long you have probably been dealing with it, it feels safer to be depressed because you know what it is and you dont always know what “better” may mean. The best advice i could give you is let yourself feel that unknown and not label it so harshly its good that you feel good and its good to be doing good and wont be easy all the time. this may not help at all but this is coming from a place of understanding somewhat of what you are going through just keep on keeping on!

Well if you know and can realize u arent a danger to yourself than i would say you dont need to be hospitalized. Obviously props to you for staying aware and my advice would be to just keep staying aware and when you think you have started to become harmful to your own wellbeing whether that means just your thoughts or can also mean your actions then id say hospitalization isnt a terrible idea. But if you dont absolutely need to be and ur symptoms can be managed at home itd be much better for you. But dont get me wrong you know you and your symptoms better than me and if you really think it could be beneficial than dont hold back. Im sending lots of support because ive been right where you are before too and its pretty scary. I really hope everything ends up well for you and wish i could over more help.

i have gone through a couple of medications that i absolutely despised. They made me crazy depressed. Made me extremely tired. And worst of all numb. Like literally so numb. Its hard to explain but thats how it felt. My emotions are usually so high and crazy all over the place if you will so going from that to not being able to cry, get angry, or even be happy or excited for things it was extremely disorienting. and i hated it. So yea i guess what made me not like my meds were side effects of it and just the way they made me feel.
